investigations.name: autopoiesis
investigations.title: Autopoiesis
investigations.objective: The paper's §Self-organized processes section states the autopoiesis criterion as a boundary problem, not a bookkeeping one: "A membrane alone is insufficient: a vesicle may form a boundary without constituting a living system. A stronger criterion is that the processes inside the boundary collectively contribute to maintaining the organization that, in turn, keeps those processes possible." This study puts that criterion on a 2D lattice and asks the discriminating question directly: does a membrane PERSIST because an internal production loop -- gated on the boundary itself staying topologically closed -- replenishes the membrane against decay, and does a mere vesicle with no such loop, from the identical seed, DISSIPATE? The two composites differ in exactly one variable (the production rate constant k_prod), so the contrast between persistence and collapse is the finding. beer2024deriving's viability bounds -- constraints on a shared state that must be maintained for the composition to persist -- are the frame: closure here is that the membrane's own maintenance is conditioned on the boundary it maintains, so break the boundary and the maintenance cannot fire.
investigations.claim:
The paper's §Self-organized processes autopoiesis criterion -- a membrane persists because the processes inside the boundary maintain the organization that keeps those processes possible -- is IMPLEMENTED here as an AUTHORED operational-closure criterion and its consequences are tested. The closure-dependence is hand-coded (production is gated by a global binary_fill_holes topological observer), NOT emergent from local physics; the persistence, knockout, and puncture results all follow from that construction, and are worthwhile because the criterion is implemented and its consequences are verified -- not because closure arose on its own. A scalar membrane field under reaction-diffusion, with production gated on the boundary staying topologically closed and self-limited by enclosed area, PERSISTS: enclosed interior area plateaus at ~149 px (homeostasis, down from the ~465 px seed) with persists == 1.0 and no collapse within a ~1800-step window. The single-variable negative control (k_prod=0, the production loop knocked out, identical seed and wiring) COLLAPSES: closure is lost by step ~96, enclosed_area -> 0, persists == 0.0. Flipping one rate constant flips persistence into dissipation, so within this authored construction the production loop is what maintains the boundary -- confirmed independently by a fatal-puncture viability bound (beer2024deriving): breaking the boundary so nothing is enclosed shuts off the closure-gated production, and the ring cannot rebuild from nothing. The boundaries of the claim are stated as findings: the homeostatic plateau is metastable, not eternal (the physically-correct signature of a closed system with no external influx, not a defect); the reaction-diffusion physics has no RNG, so persistence is deterministic and NOT seed-dependent (the multi-seed range is a degenerate single point); and this is a minimal self-maintaining boundary, NOT real membrane chemistry or metabolism. The v1 maintenance gate is an authored global topological test, and the mechanistically-local version that removes it is NO LONGER just a named next step -- it is built and measured here as v2 (see below).

MECHANISM-LEVEL UPGRADE (v2, ProtocellV2, answering peer-review M4). v2 removes the global observer entirely -- production depends on a LOCAL interior precursor field p, k_prod*phi*p*(1-phi/phi_max), and binary_fill_holes appears ONLY as a passive enclosed_area readout, never in the update (asserted structurally on the update's referenced names). Closure-dependence EMERGES from geometry -- the membrane secretes precursor (s_p*phi) and is a barrier to it (mobility Mp*(1-alpha*phi) drops inside the membrane), so a CLOSED ring confines the precursor it secretes into the enclosed pocket (measured -- interior precursor pools from ~0 to ~72 by step 1000) and sustains itself, while an OPEN ring bleeds it. MEASURED this build -- the v2 closed loop SUSTAINS topological closure ~2451 internal steps (metastable, the same order as v1's ~2450-2650 window, but with no global observer in the loop; enclosed_area declines 465 -> 0 as the membrane thickens inward -- a long metastable transient, not an eternal fixed point), while the PRECURSOR knockout s_p=0 (the new mechanistic single-variable control) collapses at ~step 95, ~26x faster, as does k_prod=0. The PUNCTURE is now a genuine local PREDICTION, not a restatement -- zeroing a 60-degree wedge of the steady ring makes the interior precursor bleed out through the gap and the wedge membrane starves LOCALLY (punctured-wedge mass stays ~2 versus ~79 in the intact ring at the same step) and never self-heals. So EMERGE is upgraded from authored-closure to genuinely-emergent local-mechanism closure. What v2 does NOT do -- reach steady self-maintenance: the plateau is still METASTABLE (a closed budget). The open-system driven version (v2-open, ProtocellV2Open) is BUILT AND MEASURED, and the honest verdict is that a local external drive does NOT sustain closure indefinitely -- it DESTABILISES the ring into faster runaway filling (closure lost ~step 591 vs the undriven ~2451; no local drive in an ~80-point sweep reaches a bounded steady enclosed_area), while the controls confirm the drive does not rescue closure. So EMERGE stays at genuinely-emergent-but-metastable closure, NOT upgraded to steady self-maintenance.

investigations.name: biomolecular-complementarity
investigations.title: Biomolecular Complementarity
investigations.objective: The paper's §Molecular compositions section (Fig 7) frames its subject as a question about interfaces, not architecture: which patterns of molecular complementarity give rise to interfaces that behave as functional, regulatable boundaries, and which produce transient or unregulated aggregates? This study puts two spatial primitives of that question on the lattice. Differential-adhesion cell sorting -- Steinberg's Differential Adhesion Hypothesis -- is complementarity made spatial: a mixed population of two cell types, distinguished only by which contacts they find energetically favorable, demixes so that like sits with like and the heterotypic boundary between them collapses, a direct spatial reading of which interface variables must align for two cells to stay coupled. Biomolecular-condensate phase separation is the diffuse-interface counterpart: a scalar composition field, seeded near-critical, spontaneously separates into two phases divided by a sharp interface -- a boundary forming out of a well-mixed medium, the way a condensate droplet does. Each is a real 2D spatial mechanism run through the process-bigraph engine; the two are independent demonstrations, not one coupled model.
investigations.claim: Differential-adhesion cell sorting reproduces the paper's §Molecular compositions complementarity (Fig 7) as a spatial mechanism: two cell types differing only in which contacts they find energetically favorable demix a well-mixed checkerboard (heterotypic-interface fraction ~0.64 -> ~0.06 over ~600 Monte Carlo steps) while staying cohesive (live-cell pixels ~1530, <1% drift; per-type counts constant at 32/32) -- like sitting with like is the spatial reading of which interface variables must align for coupling. Independently, a Cahn-Hilliard composition field realizes the condensate mechanism the paper draws from banani2017: a near-critical field phase-separates into two domains bounded by a sharp, emergent interface (variance ~7e-5 -> ~0.38 over 10000 steps) with mass conserved to ~4e-18 and the field bounded in [-1, 1]. The honest boundary of the claim is explicit: the condensate forms an interface but does not yet do interface work -- it does not selectively concentrate or exclude a second species -- so it demonstrates a boundary forming, not yet the functional, regulatable boundary the paper's central question distinguishes from a transient aggregate. Neither regime computes a binding affinity; both are tuned demonstration primitives, not fitted to a measured tissue or condensate. The two run as independent processes through the process-bigraph engine, with no coupling between them.

investigations.name: cell-cell-coupling
investigations.title: Cell–Cell Coupling
investigations.objective:
Does the paper's §Cell–cell coupling viability-negotiation pattern (no dedicated
figure) hold as real spatial multicellularity — multiple CPM cells sharing one diffusing
nutrient field, each running its own dynamic-FBA step at its own footprint, producing both
resource preemption between two cells and cross-feeding — when the whole colony is composed from independent
frameworks through one N-cell coupling process (`CpmColonyField`), rather than the lumped
two-role, shared-scalar-pool stand-in a lumped, specification-stage realization used?
investigations.claim:
Composing N real CPM cells with one shared, real spatio-flux nutrient field through a
single N-cell coupling process (`CpmColonyField`) reproduces the paper's §Cell–cell coupling
viability-negotiation pattern (no dedicated figure) as genuine spatial multicellularity, not a
scripted or lumped stand-in for it: over
20-tick runs, an uptake-capacity asymmetry alone (glucose_vmax 10 vs 4) drives asymmetric
growth via resource preemption between the two cells (biomass ratio 2.9-3.7x across 5 seeds,
3.69x on the flagship seed; volume 3511 vs 81
px — the loser displaced but still viable, above its 1.25 seed, not driven below a viability
bound; the dividing-population lift (M7b, `cellcell-compete-div`) turns this into robust competitive DOMINANCE — fast lineage ~9x the slow's biomass, monoculture-controlled — with full exclusion only stochastic, so exclusion is earned only as a seed-dependent outcome, not deterministically, and the winner's ~97.5%-lattice swell without division is a saturation artifact), while a
different composite over the same coupling process — a localized glucose depot, a fast-diffusing
acetate byproduct, and an acetate-consuming role — sustains a cell that never touches glucose
(local glucose 0.0) purely via a diffusing cross-feeding handoff (local acetate 1.30, biomass
1.25 -> 3.79). Both regimes run through the same process; only the composite's cell roles and
field constants differ, mirroring the lumped ODE predecessor's law-4 pattern
(two handler environments negotiate the shared-resource constraint differently over one
interface) at real spatial, per-footprint metabolic resolution.

investigations.name: cell-environment-coupling
investigations.title: Cell–Environment Coupling (flagship)
investigations.objective:
When a single cell metabolizes at its own location, does it measurably reshape the very
nutrient gradient it depends on — environmental modification (local resource depletion + secretion) — closing the paper's
§Cell–environment coupling sense → metabolize → secrete loop (Fig 4) as real spatial
metabolism: one cell sensing local glucose, running flux-balance analysis at its own footprint,
growing, and secreting a byproduct that diffuses back into the field it senses? The paper
frames this feedback loop as "the minimal structure required for control"; here the loop is
genuinely closed (a real depletion → uptake feedback) in the flagship, while directed control —
chemotaxis up the sensed gradient — is the flagship's non-motile-by-design other half, now
BUILT and MEASURED in the `chemotaxis` variant (finding F-08). Mechanistically, the cell and its environment are
two real, independently-built simulators (viva-cpm's Cellular Potts engine, spatio-flux's
diffusion-advection and dynamic-FBA processes) composed through one typed coupling process
(`CpmCellField`), rather than a scripted or lumped stand-in for that coupling.
investigations.claim:
Composing a real CPM cell with a real spatio-flux nutrient field through one typed
coupling process (`CpmCellField`) reproduces the paper's §Cell–environment coupling
sense → metabolize → secrete loop (Fig 4) as genuine spatial metabolism, not a scripted stand-in
for it (the flagship loop is closed; directed control/chemotaxis is built and measured in the
`chemotaxis` variant, finding F-08) — over 20 ticks the
cell runs dynamic-FBA at its own
footprint (`e_coli_core`, O2-capped to force acetate overflow), grows ~3.4x in CPM volume (32
-> 110 px, ~3% of a 60x60 lattice it does not come close to filling), depletes local glucose by
up to ~18% peak-to-trough (~6% from the initial condition) before diffusion partially resupplies it
(environmental modification), and secretes a
diffusing acetate plume — two independently-built simulators talking through one typed port.

investigations.name: cellular-interface
investigations.title: The Cellular Interface
investigations.objective: Can the cellular boundary be specified as nothing but typed, unit-bearing exchange ports (chemical mol·s⁻¹, mechanical N, electrical C·s⁻¹, thermal J·s⁻¹) plus higher-level variables (growth, shape, objective, viability) — with no committed mechanism — and compiled, by installing one conforming handler, into a bounded, goal-directed cell whose interface is exactly the one declared?
investigations.claim: The cell's interface is authored as an inert typed contract and compiled to a running bounded cell; a non-conforming handler that breaks the port contract is rejected at compile time with a CompileError naming the missing ports (Law 1 conformance).

investigations.name: development-and-evolution
investigations.title: Development and Evolution
investigations.objective: The paper's §Development and evolution section (Fig 10c-f) extends the interface idea across time: individual cellular interfaces become embedded in a COLLECTIVE interface defined by shared state -- a growing colony develops physiological heterogeneity (a depleted core against a fed rim) where each cell's own interface sits inside one collective interface -- and a heritable trait EVOLVES when variation is selected on that shared field. This study puts both halves on the real dividing CPM colony and asks the discriminating question directly: does a growing CPM colony on a shared depleting glucose field form emergent core-vs-rim heterogeneity (DEVELOPMENT), and does a heritable per-cell glucose-uptake trait (vmax) shift its population mean UP under shared-field selection (EVOLUTION) -- and, crucially, is that directional shift caused by SELECTION rather than mutation alone? The design is a DUAL control: against the selection-ON colony, a no-mutation arm (the trait cannot vary) and a no-selection arm (the trait mutates but confers no fitness) test whether selection, not mutation or drift, drives it. This study REUSES study 8's dividing colony (`growth-and-division`, `CpmGrowthDivision`) unchanged and adds ONLY one heritable coupling parameter -- the paper's claim that the interfaces and couplings are themselves evolvable features of organization, made concrete by making one coupling parameter heritable and selectable on the colony that already grows and divides.
investigations.claim: The paper's §Development and evolution section (Fig 10c-f) holds as a spatial mechanism on the real dividing CPM colony, REUSING study 8's `CpmGrowthDivision` unchanged and adding only a heritable per-cell coupling parameter. DEVELOPMENT: a growing colony on a shared depleting glucose field forms emergent core-vs-rim physiological heterogeneity -- the radial rim-core glucose ratio is an ENSEMBLE BAND across N=30 seeds (mean 1.283, sd 0.159, range [1.062, 1.815]; flagship seed 3 ends 1.445; every seed clears the 1.0 floor), a collective interface not imposed but emerging from shared-field competition. EVOLUTION: a heritable glucose-uptake trait (vmax) shifts its population mean UP under shared-field selection, and at N=30 seeds SELECTION is a STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT driver -- a Mann-Whitney U rank test on the per-seed deltas (selection-ON vs no-selection) gives U=685, p=5.3e-4 (rank-biserial r=+0.52, CLES 0.76), and the drift-null check rejects neutral drift (Wilcoxon p=1.2e-5); selection-ON mean delta +0.233 (sd 0.296, up 22/30). A DUAL control isolates selection -- the no-mutation control stays exactly at the founder value with zero variance (0/30, static, no raw material), and the no-selection control mutates (var > 0) but drifts undirected near zero (-0.026, up 13/30, the neutral-drift envelope). The directional up-shift appears only under selection AND is distinguishable from drift at p<0.001, so the dual control ESTABLISHES selection (not mutation, not drift) via differential division on the shared field (higher-vmax cells grow/divide more, so their trait proliferates) -- upgrading the earlier n=5 "consistent with" reading; the effect is medium and the shift modest (+0.23 over ~4 generations). The gate is re-leveled onto this ensemble rank test, off the flagship seed 3 (kept only as a regression pin). The boundaries are stated as findings: the development and evolution halves pull the same field-depletion knob and both saturate within the ~gen 4-6 crowding window; the scope is a toy evo-devo (development = shared-field core/rim heterogeneity, NOT morphogenesis; evolution = one scalar trait under resource selection, NOT genome evolution; facilitated variation -- evolving the ports/couplings themselves -- is a named deferral).

investigations.name: disintegration
investigations.title: Disintegration
investigations.objective:
Does the paper's §Disintegration level-shift (Fig 5) hold spatially -- a coherent CPM cell that loses structural
viability when a diffusing field of acetate (the SAME metabolic byproduct that is waste-and-food
in `cell-cell-coupling`, here toxic at high local concentration) crosses its viability
bound, its domain resorbing while its shed material becomes scattering physical particles -- composed from independent frameworks
(viva-cpm + spatio-flux particles) through one coupling process (`CpmDisintegration` +
`BrownianMovement`)?
investigations.claim:
Composing one real CPM cell with a real spatio-flux acetate field and a real spatio-flux
particle-movement process through two coupling processes (`CpmDisintegration` for the
viability-collapse trigger and resorption, stock `BrownianMovement` for the debris scatter)
reproduces the paper's §Disintegration level-shift (Fig 5) as spatial dissolution with a SCRIPTED
resorption schedule (resorb_per_tick=6.0): the trigger timing is simulation-derived (the
footprint-local acetate crossing a viability bound), the resorption ramp itself is scripted -- not a
lumped scalar stand-in: over a fixed-seed deterministic 20-tick CPM run, the cell holds coherent
(area > 30) through tick 6, the footprint-local acetate mean crosses viability_threshold at
released_tick = 7, the domain resorbs to area 0 by tick 16, and its 63 shed pixels become a
debris cloud whose RMS spread strictly increases through tick 24 (the trajectory -- hold, cross,
resorb, particle count -- reproduces exactly; the scatter cloud moves under unseeded
`BrownianMovement`, so its exact RMS magnitudes are representative of one run, not
run-to-run-reproducible -- only the strict-increase direction is the robust claim) -- hold,
cross, resorb, scatter, end to end from one coupling process plus one stock movement process,
mirroring a lumped, specification-stage realization's §Disintegration level-shift pattern (Fig 5) at
real spatial, per-pixel resolution.

investigations.name: fig-01
investigations.title: fig-01: Interfaces & composition
investigations.objective: Is the paper's definitional Fig 1 (§Interfaces and composition, Fig composition_framework) executable rather than merely drawn -- does the smallest honest process bigraph, one typed process wired through ports to two nested place-graph stores, actually run and move quantity from a source store to a sink store while conserving the total?
investigations.claim: The paper's definitional Fig 1 is executable, not merely drawn: the minimal process bigraph -- one typed `StoreTransfer` process wired through a `source` input port and `source`/`sink` output ports to two scalar place-graph stores -- runs forward under the process-bigraph engine and moves quantity from source `store_a` to sink `store_b` while conserving the total. Because the transfer is fixed-rate deterministic (k=0.15, interval 1.0), the trajectory is exact: store_a[n] == 0.85^n (draining from 1.0 to ~0.0388 over 20 ticks), store_b[n] == 1 - 0.85^n (filling as its complement), the sink overtakes the source at tick 5, and store_a + store_b == 1.0 to round-off at every tick. This is the dynamics behind the figure's static signature -- a process reading and writing shared variables through ports wired to stores in a place graph -- shown to actually run.

investigations.name: fig-02
investigations.title: fig-02: Orchestration
investigations.objective: Is the paper's orchestration claim (Fig orchestration, panel a) executable rather than merely drawn -- does a runnable process-bigraph composite in which two processes update at DIFFERENT rates through ONE shared store actually reproduce multi-timescale coordination: the fast process filling the shared pool far more often than the slow one converts it, the two rates coordinated through the shared store, and the combined trajectory reflecting both timescales while conserving mass?
investigations.claim: The paper's multi-timescale orchestration claim (Fig orchestration, panel a) is executable, not merely drawn: composing a fast process and a slow process through ONE shared `pool` store, each updating on its own interval, reproduces panel (a)'s "processes that update at different rates through a shared store" as a runnable, deterministic trajectory. Over a fixed 20-tick run the fast process updates the shared store on every tick (20 changes) while the slow process converts only 3 times, `molecules` is a sawtooth (rises on the fast clock, drawn down at each slow firing), `biomass` advances monotonically in a coarse staircase on the slow clock (levels 0 -> 3.0 -> 7.2 -> 11.88, never returning to the pool), and mass is conserved through the shared store across both timescales -- at every tick `molecules + biomass` equals the cumulative fast injection (== elapsed time), ending 8.12 + 11.88 = 20.0. The combined trajectory reflects both timescales at once; the composite is didactic and uncalibrated, so this demonstrates the ORCHESTRATION MECHANISM, not any biological magnitude.

investigations.name: fig-03
investigations.title: fig-03: The cellular interface
investigations.objective: The paper's §Cellular interface (Fig cell_interface) defines a cell as an organization that senses and acts on its environment through typed PORTS -- "each port is a typed connection from the cell to a single variable in the shared state, with a type that fixes the units of what crosses it." Fig cell_interface a. shows interaction modalities as ports (nutrient exchange, motile force, growth, electrical signaling); Fig cell_interface b. shows a minimal interface combining physical exchange ports with higher-level cellular variables (growth, shape, objectives, viability bounds). Is that interface EXECUTABLE rather than merely drawn -- i.e. does a runnable process-bigraph composite exercise those typed ports so that each port's value RESPONDS to its driving environmental input, demonstrating the typed cell -> shared-variable connection the caption asserts?
investigations.claim: Fig cell_interface is executable: composing one bounded cell (`CellularInterfaceHandler`) with a four-driver environment through the `fig03-runnable` composite exercises the caption's typed interface ports so that each port's value responds to its driving input, demonstrating the typed cell -> shared-variable connection the paper asserts. Deterministically: a 5x higher chemical supply (0.2 -> 1.0) produces exactly a 5x larger uptake flux (-0.16 -> -0.80) and a strictly larger Monod growth rate (0.171 -> 0.400); the mechanical, electrical, and thermal exchange ports each respond linearly to their own driver and read zero when it is off; the cell accretes shape (volume 1.0 -> 10.6) as it grows over the 24-step run; and with the thermal driver held at 45 C (above the 37 C optimum) viability falls strictly monotonically from 1.0 to 0.175 by Arrhenius thermal death, whereas at the 37 C optimum it barely moves (1.0 -> 0.911, a decline < 0.1) -- isolating temperature as the cause. Every number is a deterministic function of the handler's response laws and reproduces exactly run to run.

investigations.name: fig-04
investigations.title: fig-04: Cell–environment coupling
investigations.objective: Is the paper's §Cell-environment coupling figure (Fig cell_environment) executable — does a runnable process-bigraph composite actually close the control loop the caption asserts, where an environmental chemical field DRIVES the cell's interface ports (sensing, uptake, growth, motility) and the cell acts back on that shared field? Concretely: does a real diffusing nutrient gradient, sensed locally at an interior grid index, drive uptake that tracks the sensed field, grow the cell's mass, and pull it up-gradient (chemotaxis) — env field → sensed value → uptake → mass gain, plus up-gradient drift — all as measured simulation output, not a drawn diagram?
investigations.claim: The paper's §Cell-environment coupling figure is executable, not merely drawn: the `fig04-runnable` composite closes the caption's control loop as measured simulation output. A real diffusing nutrient gradient, sensed locally at interior grid index 4, drives the cell's interface ports — uptake is linear in the local sensed field (exactly 4× the field ⇒ 4× the uptake; per-step uptake tracks the sensed field at correlation 1.0), mass grows monotonically (1.0 → ~1.432 over 24 steps), and the cell drifts up-gradient (index 4.0 → ~4.196, net +0.196). The cell writes its uptake back into the shared environment store, closing the sense→act loop, and the mass↔uptake ledger closes exactly (Δmass == 0.5 × cumulative uptake booked to the env). A zero-field negative control gives zero drive on every port, establishing the field as the causal driver. All values are deterministic run-to-run (no RNG in the composite). These are toy-real, uncalibrated magnitudes — the calibrated spatial cousin is `cell-environment-coupling` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation.

investigations.name: fig-05
investigations.title: fig-05: Disintegration
investigations.objective: Does the paper's §Disintegration Fig 5b grain swap hold as a runnable composite -- a viability signal driving a control that toggles between a coarse cellular process and a fine molecular one realizing the same interface, so that crossing the viability bound replaces the coarse description with the finer one? Concretely: as an external stress ramp slides viability across a threshold, does a GrainSelector flip the active grain coarse->fine at the crossing, and does the shared biomass output turn over from growth (coarse, alive) to decay (fine, dying) at the switch?
investigations.claim: Composing a `StressRamp`, a `GrainSelector`, and two gated grain processes (`CoarseGrainProcess`, `FineGrainProcess`) sharing one biomass/energy interface reproduces Fig 5b's viability-driven grain swap as a runnable temporal study: over a deterministic 26-step run, viability declines monotonically across the 0.5 threshold, the GrainSelector flips the active grain coarse->fine at the crossing (t=13, one tick after viability first reads below threshold at t=12), exactly one grain acts per tick, and the shared biomass output turns over from linear growth (coarse, alive; peak 3.9 at the flip) to first-order decay (fine, dying; ~1.14 by t=26). This is a didactic, uncalibrated realization of the level shift the paper draws -- the coarse cellular description being replaced by the finer molecular one as the cell crosses its viability bound.

investigations.name: fig-06
investigations.title: fig-06: The molecular interface
investigations.objective: Does the paper's §Molecular interfaces figure (Fig molecular_interface) hold as a runnable process -- a molecular mechanism (F₁Fₒ ATP synthase) that exchanges matter and energy through a small set of TYPED physical channels (chemical mol·s⁻¹, electrical C·s⁻¹, mechanical torque N·m, thermal J·s⁻¹) with NO cell-level boundary, all four channels driven from ONE coupled proton flux so matter, charge, angular momentum, and energy are conserved across the interface?
investigations.claim: The F₁Fₒ ATP synthase modeled as a single molecular process with four TYPED physical ports (chemical `chemical_flux`, electrical `current`, mechanical `torque`, thermal `heat_flux`) over a `structure` leaf -- and NO cell boundary -- reproduces the paper's §Molecular interfaces figure (Fig molecular_interface) as a runnable transducer: driven by one ramped proton flux, the mechanism emits an ATP synthesis flux that scales linearly with the drive (`J_ATP = k_cat·activity`, exactly 4× flux for 4× activity), a proton current fixed to that flux at the ATP:H⁺ = 1/3.3 stoichiometry on every step, a near-constant rotary torque of 4×10⁻²⁰ N·m, and a dissipated heat exactly equal to (1−η)·PMF-power = 25 % of input power -- so matter (chemical), charge (electrical), angular momentum (mechanical), and energy (thermal) are conserved across one coupled interface, all four channels derived from the single proton flux, all deterministic and reproducible run to run.

investigations.name: fig-07
investigations.title: fig-07: Nested cellular hierarchy
investigations.objective: Does the paper's §Biomolecular compositions figure (Fig molecular_compositions) hold as an executable composite -- can molecular structures organized hierarchically across scales (proteins to complexes, organelles, ECM) be represented as a NESTED place graph, with processes that interact with those nested states corresponding to cellular compartments and structures, such that a process acting at one nesting level actually moves quantity in a deeply-nested store while the place-graph containment is preserved as the whole cell evolves as one coupled system?
investigations.claim: Wiring six ODE processes over one place graph whose stores nest up to six levels deep -- WITHOUT flattening the compartment hierarchy -- reproduces the paper's §Biomolecular compositions figure (Fig molecular_compositions) as a runnable nested cascade: over a deterministic 30-step run, a process acting at each nesting level moves quantity in its nested store (transport fills cytoplasmic nutrients 0 -> 9.0; metabolism makes metabolites 0 -> ~20.5 and energy 0 -> ~13.1; transcription reads the six-levels-deep DNA to make RNA 0 -> ~0.64; translation makes protein 0 -> ~0.24; subunit assembly grows the four-levels-deep ribosome pool 0.5 -> ~0.88, closing the loop; replication / repair holds the six-levels-deep genome at DNA == 1.0), and the place-graph containment is preserved as the dynamics run -- the deep stores stay nested inside their parents, reachable only at full depth, alongside their untouched siblings. The whole hierarchy evolves as one coupled cell; every value reproduces exactly run to run.

investigations.name: fig-08
investigations.title: fig-08: Self-organized processes
investigations.objective: Is the paper's Fig. self_organized_process (§Composition of the cellular interface) executable rather than merely drawn -- does the `fig08-runnable` composite actually demonstrate that a cellular interface EMERGES when molecular processes are compositionally coupled so they maintain one another (metabolism synthesizes the components the membrane and replication need, containment/expression maintain the pools metabolism needs), so that the coupled system holds a sustained, far-from-equilibrium balance rather than each process running down independently?
investigations.claim: Fig. self_organized_process is executable: the `fig08-runnable` composite couples containment, metabolism, gene expression, replication, diffusion, and mass-action reactions over ten shared flat building-block pools, and over a deterministic 40-tick run it demonstrates the caption's exact principle -- the coupled processes maintain one another into a sustained, far-from-equilibrium balance (every pool strictly positive and bounded; template/catalytic pools genes, energy, metabolites, nucleic_acids hold steady within 25% while structural material membrane, proteins, enzymes is net-produced), and that balance is a property of the COUPLING, not of any pool in isolation: removing metabolism starves its downstream metabolite pool toward zero and freezes energy at its seed, and removing gene expression freezes the enzyme pool metabolism depends on and drops metabolism's metabolite output. This is a toy-real didactic demonstration, not a calibrated model; its rigorous cousin is the `autopoiesis` study in `draft-to-living-cell`.

investigations.name: fig-09
investigations.title: fig-09: Growth & division
investigations.objective: Does the paper's §Growth-and-division claim (Fig. division) hold as a runnable composite -- that division is a compositional rewrite in which "one maintained boundary becomes two, with stores partitioned across daughters and interface ports duplicated" (caption a: DNA replication, elongation, septum, separation; caption b: "division ... partitions state variables such as DNA and biomass into two cells") -- when realized as a genuine place-graph rewrite over a colony `tree[node]` store driven through the process-bigraph engine?
investigations.claim: Realizing the paper's Fig. division caption b as a genuine place-graph rewrite over a colony `tree[node]` store (one `CellCycleDivision` process alternating REPLICATE and DIVIDE rewrites, driven through the process-bigraph engine) reproduces "division ... partitions state variables such as DNA ... into two cells": over a deterministic 12-tick run the founder cell replicates its chromosome (DNA store doubles 1.0 -> 2.0 while the boundary count stays 1) then divides (one cell becomes two, each daughter carrying one chromosome with dna 1.0), and repeats to 4 cells -- and at every division event the boundary count exactly doubles, the total DNA store is conserved across the rewrite (2.0 -> 2x1.0; 4.0 -> 4x1.0, nothing created or destroyed), and each daughter inherits exactly half of a parent cell's DNA. Replication always precedes division. This is a toy-real, uncalibrated didactic composite -- the division trigger is a discrete cell-cycle clock reaching a replicated (two-chromosome) state, not an integrated biomass threshold -- whose point is to make "division is a compositional rewrite" literally executable, not to reproduce division kinetics.

investigations.name: fig-10
investigations.title: fig-10: Development
investigations.objective: Is the paper's §Development figure (Fig development) executable -- can a runnable process-bigraph composite demonstrate, under test, that development is "a hierarchical reorganization where individual cells become part of a collective composite" rather than merely more cells? Concretely: does running the `fig10-emergence` composite turn a set of free motile bacteria (top-level place-graph siblings) into a nested biofilm microcolony that then secretes an extracellular matrix -- surface attachment, ECM secretion, growth of a structured community (caption a) realized as a genuine runtime place-graph rewrite (caption b)?
investigations.claim: The paper's §Development figure (Fig development) is executable, not merely drawn: running the `fig10-emergence` composite performs a genuine runtime place-graph rewrite that turns four free motile bacteria (top-level siblings) into a nested biofilm microcolony that then secretes an extracellular matrix -- "individual cells become part of a collective composite" (caption b) via "surface attachment, ECM secretion, growth of structured communities" (caption a). Over a deterministic 16-step run: all four free cells attach at once at t=6 (free 4 -> 0, biofilm-nested 0 -> 4) as a new `biofilm` collective node appears and the cells' place-graph depth increases from 1 to 2 and never reverts; ECM is absent until maturation and then accumulates to 3 nodes over t=12..14, only while the sessile community exists. This is a hierarchical reorganization -- a re-parenting into a collective with its own shared state -- not merely more cells. Two companion rewrites exercised by the same suite (cell-cycle division 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 with true chromosome partition; biofilm-to-capacity + ECM, and a mutant lineage sweeping a wildtype population) confirm the same principle across the section's neighboring transformations. The composites are toy-real and uncalibrated; the calibrated spatial cousin is `development-and-evolution` in `draft-to-living-cell`.

investigations.name: fig-11
investigations.title: fig-11: Evolution
investigations.objective: Does the paper's §Evolution figure (Fig 11) hold as a runnable place-graph rewrite -- a top-level population of identically-schema'd cells, each exposing a scalar trait, evolving over generations toward a selection optimum set by the environmental niche, so that (Fig 11b) the trait distribution shifts toward the optimum via binary fission + heritable mutation + selection, while division itself (Fig 11a) is a discrete event that REPLACES a parent cell with two daughters?
investigations.claim: Composing one `population` (`tree[node]` of identically-schema'd `cell` nodes) with one `environment` niche through a single `PopulationEvolution` process reproduces the paper's §Evolution pattern (Fig 11) as a runnable place-graph rewrite: over a fixed-seed (seed=1) 40-generation run the founder cell (trait 0.0, a gap of 1.0 below the niche optimum) divides by binary fission -- the parent REPLACED by two mutated daughters -- grows to carrying capacity (12) and never exceeds it, while the selection optimum drifts monotonically from 1.0 to 1.80 and the population mean trait climbs from 0.0 to ~1.68, closing the trait-optimum gap from 1.0 to ~0.12. The distribution shifts toward the environmental optimum via variation (mutation) + heritability + selection, and division edits the place graph (parent id gone, two fresh daughter ids present) -- the whole trajectory is deterministic and reproduces exactly run to run. This is a didactic, toy-real illustration of the Darwinian loop, not a calibrated population-genetics model.

investigations.name: growth-and-division
investigations.title: Growth and Division
investigations.objective:
A cell grows, crosses a threshold, and divides -- and its daughters do not necessarily divide together. This is the paper's §Growth and division growth-then-divide pattern (Fig 10a,b): metabolism drives a cell's own state across a threshold, crossing it fires division and partitions state across the two resulting daughters, and those daughters, "remain[ing] coupled through shared environmental state," can either stay in step or diverge (§Growth and division).
Does this hold spatially -- a single CPM cell whose metabolism (dFBA solved at its own lattice footprint) grows its volume until it crosses `vol_threshold` and divides via the native CPM engine operation `divide_cells`, partitioning biomass mass-conserved across the two daughters, compounding into a small multi-generation lineage tree -- and do sibling cells sharing one glucose field begin growing at different local rates as the colony crowds, so their division timing desynchronizes rather than staying locked to clean powers of two? Composed from independent frameworks (viva-cpm + spatio-flux + cobra) through one coupling process (`CpmGrowthDivision`).
investigations.claim: Metabolism-driven growth crossing a threshold fires division, and division partitions state -- biomass, and lattice pixels -- across two daughters that resume growing themselves, compounding into a genuine multi-generation lineage tree whose siblings desynchronize as they compete for shared, local resources: this is the paper's §Growth and division growth-then-divide pattern (Fig 10a,b), including its "coordination and divergence" clause, realized spatially. One real CPM cell, growing via real per-footprint dFBA metabolism, divides via the native CPM engine operation `divide_cells` (biomass partitioned proportional to post-split daughter volume, not reset and discarded) through a single coupling process (`CpmGrowthDivision`). Over a 36-tick run sampled every 3 ticks: the founder compounds into an 18-cell lineage tree spanning 4 generations (`max_generation` = 4), the population steps up in a monotonic non-decreasing staircase (1,2,2,2,4,4,5,8,8,11,14,18) that departs from clean powers of two from tick 21 onward as sibling cells' division timing diverges, and every cell's CPM volume stays bounded in a sawtooth between `reset_target` = 40 and `vol_threshold` = 80. The staircase is bounded more by lattice crowding (the colony packs to roughly two-thirds occupancy within its own footprint) than by nutrient limitation (field-wide glucose depletes only ~3% over the run). This is direct simulation output from three independently-developed frameworks (viva-cpm + spatio-flux + cobra) meeting at one typed interface. It mirrors a lumped, specification-stage realization's §Growth and division claim (Fig 10a,b) (growth drives the cell's own state across a threshold; crossing the threshold triggers division) but realizes division as the native spatial CPM operation `divide_cells` acting directly on lattice pixels, in contrast to that study's place-graph rewrite (one node becoming two structurally-new nodes at a lumped, non-spatial level of composition).

investigations.name: molecular-interfaces
investigations.title: Molecular Interfaces
investigations.objective: The paper's §Molecular interface (Fig 6) frames a molecule not as a lump of state but as a typed interface exposing several physical channels -- chemical, electrostatic, mechanical, thermal -- through which molecules bind, react, and transmit force and heat. It even names the public databases (PDB, Reactome, ChEBI, GO) as "partial specifications of molecular interfaces and their types". This study asks the discriminating question one channel down: does that molecular interface hold SPATIALLY? Concretely -- do local molecular reactions plus differential diffusion (the CHEMICAL channel spatialized as finite-amplitude, nucleation-driven Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion patterning -- not linear-instability Turing sensu stricto) turn a near-uniform seed into emergent spatial structure, and does a static uniform temperature field acting as an Arrhenius rate multiplier (no heat transport, no reaction->heat feedback) GRADE that structure -- so that a temperature PARAMETER demonstrably modulates the spatialized chemical channel over one shared spatial field? The causal control -- equal diffusion (Du = Dv), chemistry untouched -- differs in exactly one variable and isolates the diffusion asymmetry as the cause of structure (a regime-specific conclusion for this Gray-Scott system), so the contrast between pattern and uniformity is the finding.
investigations.claim: The paper's §Molecular interface (Fig 6) holds spatially for its CHEMICAL channel, and a temperature parameter modulates it. The CHEMICAL channel, realized as a Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion system (local autocatalysis U + 2V -> 3V plus differential diffusion Dv < Du), turns a near-uniform seed into an emergent finite-amplitude, nucleation-driven Gray-Scott spot pattern (not linear-instability Turing sensu stricto): v_var rises from ~0.0011 to ~0.0119 with ~12 connected domains (patterned == 1.0). The equal-diffusion causal control (Du = Dv = 0.12, chemistry unchanged -- the single differing variable) stays UNIFORM (v_var ~= 0, patterned == 0.0), so the pattern is CAUSED by the diffusion asymmetry, not the chemistry alone -- a regime-specific conclusion for this Gray-Scott system. A static uniform temperature field acting as an Arrhenius rate multiplier exp(-Ea*(1/T - 1/Tref)) (no heat transport, no reaction->heat feedback) GRADES the pattern (Ea=0.15, T=1.2: ~12 domains -> ~2, v_var ~0.0119 -> ~0.0096) while staying patterned: a temperature parameter modulating the chemical channel, not a second physically-transported channel and not a collapse. Multi-seed (seeds 1-5, physics is deterministic so the seed is re-drawn into the initial field): v_var in [0.01157, 0.01193], n_domains in [8, 12] -- reported as a range. The boundaries are findings, not caveats: the ELECTROSTATIC and MECHANICAL channels are the named four-modality gap; the databases claim (PDB/Reactome/ChEBI/GO as partial specifications of molecular-interface types) is realized as an ILLUSTRATIVE typed-port annotation over the Gray-Scott species, not a resolved mapping; and this is a toy reaction-diffusion demonstration, not real molecular structure or conformation.
